grammar.title: Pedidos e permissão: can, could, may
grammar.explanation_pt:
Você já usa **can** para pedidos. Em situações formais (hotel, aeroporto, trabalho), suba o nível de educação:

**Pedir que alguém faça algo:**
- **Can you** help me? (neutro)
- **Could you** help me, please? (mais educado ✅)
- **Would you mind** helping me? (muito educado — note o -ing)

**Pedir permissão para você fazer algo:**
- **Can I** leave my bags here? (neutro)
- **Could I** leave my bags here? (educado)
- **May I** leave my bags here? (formal)

Sempre: **could / may + verbo base** (sem to).

**Respostas:** Sure. / Of course. / Certainly. (sim) · I'm sorry, but... / I'm afraid not. (não)

No aeroporto, você **ouve** muito **may**: "**May I** see your boarding pass?"

rows: Could you open the door, please?
Would you mind opening the door?

examples.en: I'm afraid check-in is only at 3 p.m., but you can leave your bags here.

grammar.tip_pt: Na imigração, respostas curtas e claras são melhores: "**Tourism.**" / "**Two weeks.**" / "**At a hotel in Manhattan.**" Não precisa fazer frases longas.

pronunciation.tip_pt: **Could you** se junta e vira "**kúdja**", e o L de could é mudo ("kúd"). **Would** e **should** também têm o L mudo: "wúd", "shúd".

grammar.title: Should / shouldn't + have / hurt
grammar.explanation_pt:
**Should** = deveria (conselho, recomendação). É um modal como can e will: **should + verbo base**, igual para todas as pessoas.
- You **should** drink more water.
- You **shouldn't** (should not) take antibiotics without a prescription.
- **Should** I go to the hospital? / What **should** I do?

Para dizer o que você sente, há três estruturas principais:
1. **I have a/an** + sintoma: I have **a** headache / **a** fever / **a** cold / **the** flu
2. **My** + parte do corpo + **hurts / hurt**: My back **hurts**. My feet **hurt**.
3. **I feel** / **I'm** + adjetivo: I feel dizzy. I'm sick.

Atenção: **-ache** (dor) se junta a algumas partes: headache, stomachache, toothache, backache, earache. Para garganta: **sore throat**.

examples.en: I have a sore throat and a cough. What should I take?
examples.pt: Estou com dor de garganta e tosse. O que devo tomar?

examples.en: You should rest and drink hot tea with honey.
examples.pt: Você deveria descansar e tomar chá quente com mel.

examples.en: You shouldn't drive if you feel dizzy.
examples.pt: Você não deveria dirigir se estiver tonto.

grammar.tip_pt: **Sick** nos EUA = doente ("I'm sick"). No Reino Unido, **sick** também significa "enjoado, com vontade de vomitar" ("I feel sick"). Para "doente" os britânicos preferem **ill**.

pronunciation.tip_pt: **Ache** = "êik" (o CH soa como K!): headache = "rédêik", stomachache = "stâmakêik". **Should** tem L mudo: "shúd"; **shouldn't** = "shúdent".

grammar.title: Countable / uncountable + quantifiers
grammar.explanation_pt:
**Contáveis** (countable): dá para contar — têm plural. an egg → two eggs, a tomato → tomatoes.
**Incontáveis** (uncountable): não têm plural e não usam a/an. **water, milk, rice, sugar, money, time, information, advice, news, work, bread**.

Para contar incontáveis, use uma **unidade**: a **bottle of** water, a **slice of** bread, a **piece of** advice.

**Some x any:**
- **some** → afirmativas (e ofertas/pedidos): There's **some** milk. / Would you like **some** coffee?
- **any** → negativas e perguntas: We don't have **any** eggs. / Do we have **any** butter?

**Quantidades:**
- **many** + contável (perguntas/negativas): How **many** eggs? / not **many** people
- **much** + incontável (perguntas/negativas): How **much** money? / not **much** time
- **a lot of** + os dois (principalmente afirmativas): **a lot of** friends / **a lot of** work
- **a few** + contável (alguns, poucos): **a few** tomatoes
- **a little** + incontável (um pouco): **a little** salt

rows: some eggs / a lot of eggs / a few eggs
some milk / a lot of milk / a little milk
not any eggs / not many eggs
not any milk / not much milk

grammar.tip_pt: **Advice, information, news** e **furniture** são incontáveis em inglês, mas contáveis em português! "Many informations" ❌ → "**a lot of information**" ✅. "An advice" ❌ → "**a piece of advice**" / "**some advice**" ✅.

pronunciation.tip_pt: Em frases, **some** é fraco ("sâm" → "sm") e **of** vira "âv" ou até só "â": "a bottle of water" = "a bárol â uórer", "a lot of" = "a lórâv" ou "a lóra".

reading.title: Zero-waste kitchen
reading.text: Brazil wastes a lot of food — millions of tons a year. Here are a few tips to waste less. First, make a grocery list and check what you already have. Don't buy too much bread: you can freeze some slices for later. Use old bananas in cakes or smoothies. Keep vegetables in the fridge, not in a bag. And don't throw away leftovers: a little rice and a few vegetables can become a delicious fried rice! Small changes save a lot of money, too.

grammar.title: A estrutura de uma reclamação educada
grammar.explanation_pt:
Reclamar bem em inglês é uma **habilidade social**. O segredo é ser **claro e educado** ao mesmo tempo — e usar tudo o que você aprendeu no A2:

**1. Chame a atenção com educação:** "Excuse me..." / "Sorry to bother you, but..."
**2. Suavize:** "**I'm afraid** there's a problem with..." / "**I think** there's a mistake..."
**3. Explique** (simple past + present continuous / present):
"I **ordered** the steak medium, but it**'s** very undercooked." / "The AC **isn't working** and the room **is too** hot."
**4. Peça uma solução** (could / would):
"**Could you** bring me another one?" / "**Would it be possible to** change rooms?"
**5. Feche bem:** "Thank you, I appreciate it." / "Thanks for sorting it out."

**Evite:** "This is horrible!" / "I want my money back now!" — soa agressivo e geralmente resolve menos.

rows: Excuse me, sorry to bother you...
I'm afraid there's a problem with my room.
I asked for a quiet room, but it's next to the elevator.
Could I change to another room, please?
Thank you so much, I appreciate it.

grammar.tip_pt: Respostas comuns do atendente: **"I'm so sorry about that."** / **"I'll fix that right away."** (will para decisão na hora!) / **"Let me talk to the manager."**

common_mistakes.wrong: I want to make a reclamation.
common_mistakes.right: I'd like to make a complaint.
common_mistakes.why_pt: Reclamação = complaint. Reclamation é recuperação (de terras, materiais).

common_mistakes.wrong: The food is cold! Change it!
common_mistakes.right: I'm afraid the food is cold. Could you change it, please?
common_mistakes.why_pt: Imperativo direto soa rude com atendentes.

pronunciation.tip_pt: Na reclamação, o **tom** importa tanto quanto as palavras. Fale devagar, com voz calma e entonação que sobe levemente nos pedidos: "Could you change it, please? ↗". Sorria — dá para "ouvir" o sorriso!

listening.context_pt: Uma hóspede liga para a recepção do hotel à noite.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.en: Front desk, good evening. How can I help?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.en: Hi, this is Room 508. I'm sorry to call so late, but there's a problem. The air conditioning isn't working, and it's really hot. Also, the people next door are having a party. It's very noisy.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.en: I'm so sorry. I'll call the room next door right now. Would you like to change rooms? We have a quiet room on the tenth floor.

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.en: Yes, please. That would be great.

lines.speaker: Receptionist

reading.title: How to complain (and get results)
reading.text: A customer experience study found that most unhappy customers never complain — they just don't come back. That's bad for businesses, so many companies are happy when you complain politely! Experts give this advice: complain quickly, while the problem is happening. Talk to the right person — the manager, if necessary. Be specific: "The coffee was cold" is better than "Everything was terrible." Say what you want: a new dish, a discount, a refund. And stay calm: people help nice customers more.

questions.q: What do most unhappy customers do?
questions.answer: They never complain — they just don't come back.

questions.q: When should you complain?
questions.answer: Quickly, while the problem is happening.

questions.q: Why should you be specific?
questions.answer: Because a specific complaint is clearer (e.g., "The coffee was cold").

questions.q: Why should you stay calm?
questions.answer: Because people help nice customers more.

writing.model:
Subject: Problem with my stay – Room 508

Dear Manager,
I stayed at your hotel from June 3 to 6. I'm afraid there were some problems. On the first night, the air conditioning wasn't working and the room was too hot. The next night, the room next door was very noisy. The staff were friendly and they changed my room, but I didn't sleep well for two nights. Would it be possible to get a small discount on my bill?
Thank you for your attention.
Best regards,
Tatiana Lopes

culture_note.title: "Can I speak to the manager?"
culture_note.text_pt: Nos EUA, a frase **"Can I speak to the manager?"** virou meme associado a clientes arrogantes (o famoso estereótipo "Karen"). Use-a só quando necessário — e com educação. Na maioria das vezes, o próprio atendente consegue resolver se você for gentil.

review.speaking_pt: Apresentação final do A2: fale por 2 a 3 minutos, sem ler. Use as perguntas como roteiro e procure usar todos os tempos verbais do nível.
speaking_questions: How are you these days, and what's different in your life right now?
Tell me a story about a trip or a funny moment (past simple and continuous).
Compare your city with another place you know.
What are your plans for the next year? What do you think will happen?
Tell me about a problem you had (hotel, restaurant, health) and how you solved it.
review.project_pt: **Projeto final A2 — "My trip":** grave um vídeo de 3 a 4 minutos simulando uma viagem completa em inglês: check-in no aeroporto e no hotel, um pedido em restaurante com uma reclamação educada, uma ida à farmácia e, no final, um relato do que você fez (passado) e do que vai fazer na próxima viagem (futuro). Depois, assista ao seu vídeo "This is me" do A1 e compare: quanto você evoluiu? 🚀
